panel_name: Attention and Cognitive Performance Calibration Panel
purpose: Calibrate attention-related mechanisms missing from the template system. General attentional demand and analytical/convergent cognitive performance are critical for workplace, educational, and healthcare design. Current templates cover only creative/divergent performance (CREA series).

target_templates.name: Attentional Demand/Restoration
target_templates.mechanism: General attention demand as a function of environmental complexity, noise, visual clutter. Attention restoration through nature exposure.
target_templates.architectural_relevance: All building types. The foundational attention resource that other cognitive processes draw upon. Environment can deplete or restore this resource.

target_templates.name: Convergent Cognitive Performance
target_templates.mechanism: Analytical work, sustained attention, focused problem-solving as modulated by environment. Distinct from creative/divergent performance.
target_templates.architectural_relevance: Offices, schools, healthcare. Most knowledge work is convergent (analytical reports, calculations, focused reading) not divergent (brainstorming).

constructs_to_calibrate.name: attentional_capacity_baseline
constructs_to_calibrate.description: Baseline sustained attention capacity under neutral conditions
constructs_to_calibrate.current_status: well-established in cognitive psychology, needs environmental modifiers

constructs_to_calibrate.name: attention_restoration_rate
constructs_to_calibrate.description: Rate of attention restoration through nature exposure
constructs_to_calibrate.current_status: ART theory, partially captured by VIEW1 but not parameterized

constructs_to_calibrate.name: noise_attention_decrement
constructs_to_calibrate.description: Attention performance decrease per dB above threshold
constructs_to_calibrate.current_status: acoustic templates cover speech intelligibility, not general attention

constructs_to_calibrate.name: visual_clutter_threshold
constructs_to_calibrate.description: Visual complexity level above which attention suffers

constructs_to_calibrate.name: convergent_optimal_environment
constructs_to_calibrate.description: Environmental parameters that optimize convergent (analytical) work
constructs_to_calibrate.current_status: distinct from divergent, but not parameterized

key_papers.contribution: Attention Restoration Theory. Foundational framework for understanding attention fatigue and restoration.
Nature walk improved directed attention performance. Effect size d=0.5.
Moderate noise (70dB) improved creative performance, but hurt analytical performance.
Dim lighting improved creative but not analytical performance. Task-type matters.
Office noise effects on performance. Irrelevant speech most disruptive.

population_sensitivity: Children have lower baseline attention capacity
Elderly show increased susceptibility to distraction
ADHD individuals show altered attention restoration patterns
Introverts more sensitive to environmental stimulation

pre_reading: Understand directed attention vs. soft fascination
Review convergent vs. divergent task literature
calibration_protocol: 1. Parameterize attention demand from environmental features
2. Model attention restoration time-course from nature exposure
3. Quantify noise-attention relationship across noise types
4. Define visual complexity threshold for attention decrement
5. Distinguish convergent vs. divergent optimal environments
6. Create WIS conversion from attention parameters
output_deliverables: Updated T4 template JSON with calibrated parameters
Interaction coefficients with VIEW1, acoustic templates, L templates
